# Convention Handoff Requirements Checklist: Application shell and cross-cutting UX

**Purpose**: Validate that the rules this feature fixes but does not implement are specified precisely enough for the entry that inherits them to build without re-litigating them
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: The six requirements stated here and implemented elsewhere — FR-013 and FR-023 by entry R3, FR-032 to FR-035 by the first of R3 or R4 — together with every other rule this feature fixes for entries R3 through R12. A rule that is ambiguous here is ambiguous in ten later entries.

## Requirement Consistency — hide versus disable

- [x] CHK001 Is the discriminator between "hide" (FR-011) and "disable with an inline reason" (FR-013, FR-023) stated as one rule an implementer can apply, or must it be inferred by comparing three requirements? [Conflict, Spec §FR-011, §FR-013, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK002 Does FR-023's "any action a user cannot take MUST render as a disabled control" admit hidden admin navigation as an exception, or does FR-011 contradict it as written? [Conflict, Spec §FR-023, §FR-011]
- [x] CHK003 Is "an inline reason" given placement and content requirements, so that two entries implementing it produce the same thing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK004 Are the accessible name and state requirements for a disabled control specified, given FR-023 forbids a tooltip alone as the explanation? [Gap, Spec §FR-023, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK005 Is the rule stated in terms a later entry can test — is a control "one a user cannot take" decided by role, by membership, or by any failed precondition? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023]

## Requirement Clarity — the four deferred conventions

- [x] CHK006 Is a toast's auto-dismiss duration specified, or is "auto-dismissing" the whole requirement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK007 Is manual dismissal of a toast required, permitted or forbidden? [Gap, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK008 Are toasts required to be announced to assistive technology, given FR-030 and FR-031 make that surface load-bearing elsewhere in this feature? [Gap, Spec §FR-034, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK009 Are criteria stated for which of the four kinds an event uses, or is the choice left to each implementing entry? [Clarity, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK010 Is the stacking order and any limit on simultaneous toasts specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK011 Can "skeletons matching the layout they replace" be objectively verified, or is match fidelity a judgement each entry makes for itself? [Measurability, Spec §FR-032]
- [x] CHK012 Is "data landing MUST NOT shift the layout" given a threshold, or is any shift a violation? [Measurability, Spec §FR-032]
- [x] CHK013 Is a lost connection given a detection definition, so that "Can't reach the server" has a stated trigger? [Gap, Spec §FR-035]
- [x] CHK014 Is recovery specified — what clears the banner, and whether "Reconnecting" obliges a retry cadence? [Gap, Spec §FR-035]
- [x] CHK015 Does FR-033's "nothing MUST render from a client cache" conflict with FR-002's shell persisting across navigation and US3 s7's expressly stale sidebar? [Conflict, Spec §FR-033, §FR-002, US3 s7]
- [x] CHK016 Is FR-033's scope stated — screen data only, or every rendered thing including the frame? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033]

## Ownership & Traceability of the Handoff

- [x] CHK017 Is ownership unambiguous if entries R3 and R4 are built concurrently rather than in sequence, given "whichever is built first"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-032–FR-035]
- [x] CHK018 Must the implementing entry satisfy all four conventions together, or may it implement the ones its surface exercises and leave the rest? [Clarity, Spec §FR-032–FR-035]
- [x] CHK019 Is the implementing entry required to cite these requirement IDs, so the handoff is traceable from the later spec back to this one? [Traceability, Gap]
- [x] CHK020 Is removal or update of the inline deferral marker required once a convention is implemented, so the marker does not outlive its truth? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-023, §FR-032–FR-035]
- [x] CHK021 Is there a stated requirement that a convention fixed here be verified by a test in the entry that implements it, given change gate 1 asks this feature for none? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §Requirements preamble]

## Rules Inherited Beyond the Six

- [x] CHK022 Is FR-009's "no chrome beyond the sidebar, the header and the banner slot" binding on entries R3 through R12, or only on this one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK023 Is the header's slot contract precise enough for a later entry to fill it without re-asking — what counts as one control, and may a slot hold a group? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK024 Does FR-017's "everywhere in the application" extend beyond rendered screens to notification mail and other non-screen output? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK025 Is FR-022's "This doesn't exist" binding verbatim, including capitalisation and punctuation, or is it an illustration of the tone? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK026 Is FR-030's hand-built-component exception required to be recorded where a reviewer of a later entry can find it? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK027 Is FR-024's empty-surface rule stated generally enough to apply to surfaces this feature never renders, given the project-list region is its only instance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK028 Are the requirements a later entry inherits collected anywhere a reader of that entry's spec would encounter them, rather than only in this document? [Gap, Traceability]

## Notes

- **Assisted evaluation pass, 2026-08-30.** At the reviewer's request, every item was scanned against `spec.md` and marked `[x]` only where a specific sentence in that document answered it. 32 of the 91 items across the three checklists were already satisfied; the remaining 59 were then resolved by amending `spec.md` — no requirement was added or removed, every amendment landed inside an existing FR, and the resolutions narrow `docs/product/specifications.md` rather than inventing product decisions. Where the source is silent the resolution is recorded under *Assumptions* as a default. Marks are the agent's reading and remain the reviewer's to overturn.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- This checklist deliberately does not ask whether the six deferred requirements are implemented. They are not, by design, and `checklists/requirements.md` records why. It asks only whether they are written well enough to be implemented once, correctly, by someone who was not in this conversation.
